title: Admin event telemetry handbook: RBAC v2 diffs, SSO linkage, and event taxonomy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Consolidate a playbook and canonical schema for admin-facing audit telemetry that covers RBAC v2 change capture (diff encoding), SSO/SAML-linked actor identity, and a lightweight event taxonomy suitable for high-throughput ingestion and downstream forensic/alerting use cases. Deliverables: canonical JSON event shape, compact delta encoding guidelines for role/permission edits, actor/identity enrichment rules for SSO/SAML assertions, sanitizer/redaction rules for PII, and a migration plan for existing audit producers.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical event schema document published to Confluence with examples for create/update/delete/admin actions
Delta encoding format specified with examples for role binding edits, permission toggles, and policy rollbacks
SSO/SAML actor enrichment rules documented, including fallback heuristics when assertion data is partial
A test harness (unit + integration) that validates serialization/roundtrip and size targets for compact payloads
Backwards-compatible ingestion changes verified against staging audit pipeline and dashboards updated
notes_and_tradeoffs: Opting for a compact delta encoding reduces storage and egress cost but increases producer-side CPU for diff computation; we'll benchmark CPU vs storage using representative traffic
We debated using fully normalized ledgers versus compact change frames. Chosen approach: compact change frames + optional enriched ledger entries for high-fidelity forensic needs
Redaction at producer boundary minimizes risk but may obscure forensic detail. Decision: produce raw deltas internally, redact at export endpoints and in hosted customer exports per policy

To avoid cross-tenant linkage, SAML subject identifiers will be hashed with tenant-specific salt before storage; cleartext mapping retained in ephemeral KMS-protected store for 30 days for incident investigations
progress_updates: 2026-02-15: Kickoff meeting with SecEng, Platform, and Observability. Agreed scope and initial owners.

2026-02-22: Prototype delta encoder landed in private GitHub branch (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-delta-proto/pull/12). Early benchmark shows 3.2x size reduction on role-edit-heavy traces.
2026-03-02: Design review with PM and Compliance. Feedback: include explicit actor confidence field to capture SSO assertion strength and link to idp metadata.

2026-03-08: Added SAML enrichment adapter spec with fallback rules (use email if subjectId missing; prefer persistent id if available). Draft Confluence doc created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AUDIT/Admin+Event+Telemetry+Playbook
2026-03-10: Integration test harness skeleton merged. Next: run ingestion staging job and validate dashboard mappings for admin action taxonomy
review_feedback: PM (Lucas Meyer) requested clearer SLAs for retention tiers and a mapping of event types to alert categories
Design (Maya Chong) recommended a small fixed set of displayable event attributes for Console UI to avoid expensive lookups
Compliance (Elena Novak) asked for an explicit data retention and deletion flow for raw identity mapping artifacts
open_risks: Producer adoption: multiple services must change their audit producers. Risk of inconsistent implementations. Mitigation: provide a lightweight SDK and linting tools
Cross-tenant identity leakage if hashing scheme misconfigured. Mitigation: include automated tests and require KMS key rotation policy
Size vs fidelity tradeoff may impact forensic timelines if too much redaction applied. Mitigation: tiered exports and on-demand full-verbosity exports for authorized investigations
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Publish canonical schema + delta format and SDK helpers. Ship Confluence playbook and example payloads
Phase 2: SDK adoption by 3 high-priority services and end-to-end ingestion tests to staging
Phase 3: Console integrations (compact event view) and alert mapping; update dashboards and runbook
Phase 4: Migrate remaining producers, deprecate legacy event shapes after 6-week dual-write window
